newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand ready to fight new baht attacks - report.
newsitem.headline: Thailand ready to fight new baht attacks - report.

text.p: Thailand will be alert against any fresh speculative attacks on the ailing baht after its effective defence of the currency this week, central bank governor Rerngchai Marakanond said.

Rerngchai told the Nation newspaper in an interview on Thursday that his bank was prepared to intervene in foreign exchange markets and would seek cooperation, if necessary, from other regional central banks to do the job.
"The baht volatility has been going on for several days, but we decided to fight the battle in the foreign exchange markets so that we did not have to defend the baht at home," he said.

Rerngchai said: "If necessary, we'll also ask for cooperation from other countries. You've got to understand that the speculators follow no ethical codes...in the foreign exchange markets there is no world police."
"Now the foreign exchange rates fall within the band which we try to maintain, but we cannot be careless," he said.
The governor declined to say how much Thailand had used to defend the baht on Wednesday but dealers estimated the country spent billions of dollars to shore up its currency.
The baht fell to 26.330/26.440 to the dollar early on Wednesday before the Thai central bank intervention which helped the currency close sharply firmer at 25.910/25.940.
At 0341 GMT on Friday it was quoted at 25.450/25.650.

Rerngchai said currency speculators had underestimated a joint defence mechanism that Thailand has with 11 regional countries. "We have informed the speculators all along that this cooperation exists, but they say the cooperation is only on paper."

Thailand said it defended the baht on Wednesday through concerted intervention carried out with the Monetary Authority of Singapore. Other regional banks were also suspected to have been buying the Thai currency.-- Bangkok newsroom (662)-6520642
